description: DevForgeAI phase, candidate-root, lease, command, worker and tech-stack policy. Install as <repo>/.codex/hooks.json and review it with /hooks. Codex has no ConfigChange event; that row exists on Claude only.

SubagentStart._matcher_comment: Matches every agent: the write lease is bound here, the only identity-bearing pre-write event on either provider. The sequencer refuses an agent that is not the active phase's worker, and refuses a second producer with LEASE_HELD.

hooks.statusMessage: Binding worker to the active DevForgeAI phase

PreToolUse._shell_allowlist_comment: Codex declares no permission vocabulary in hooks.json; the admitted shell surface is stated in config.codex.toml and enforced by this hook. That surface is: the five model-callable `devforgeai` operations (status, phase start, phase fail --reason, validate, promote <run>), `devforgeai run <key>` for the producer holding the run's write lease, and the provider-external Research Core runner `devforgeai-research` with exactly these ten subcommands: normalize-request, open-run, append-record, put-source, transition-run, validate-run, seal-run, render, render-handoff, resume-run. Research Core is the sole writer inside its own fence and opens no framework run, so no run need be active; any other subcommand, any call from a phase worker, and any redirect or pipeline around it are refused. Every write tool is checked against the run's candidate root and phase fence.

hooks.statusMessage: Checking a completed write against the candidate root and fence

SubagentStop._matcher_comment: Matches every agent: the dispatcher answers 0 when no run is active, and the sequencer refuses a result whose agent_type is not the active phase's worker. A narrow list would silently skip the other 17 skills' workers.
